newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares shed 0.81 pct in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares shed 0.81 pct in thin volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares lost an average 0.81 percent in quiet selling on Monday as traders took profits amid weak volume after last week's 6.2 percent surge, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed at 94,107.12, down 772.02 points, or 0.81 percent from Friday's all-time high closing of 94,879.14. It brushed a high of 96,158 in early trade and ended the morning session up 0.45 percent at 95,306.73.
Trade volume plunged to 12.96 trillion lira from Friday's 19.30 trillion.
"Activity was subdued other than a few shares and the market was generally on the selling side in the afternoon," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
He said the market awaited the Treasury's 13-month bond auction set for Tuesday to see developments in financial markets.

Bond market yields had dived in the two days following last Tuesday's auction where the Treasury succeeded in issuing first ever 13-month bonds at sharply lower yields. The index had surged 8.2 percent last Tuesday and Wednesday.
"Investors may want to keep liquidity ahead of the year-end. The issue of a five-day New Year holiday remains uncertain," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank.
The Turkish government may extend the New Year holiday to five days from December 27 to January 2 by declaring December 30 and 31 official holidays.
"If the holiday is extended, there may be purchases in the last two days of the week because payments will be delayed until after the holiday," Haydaroglu said.
"If the market establishes firm support at 94,000 levels, an upward move is possible," he added.

Of the 232 shares traded, losers outdid gainers by 110 to 70 and 52 finished stable. The 85-share industrial index eased 0.53 percent to 101,446.36 and the 15-share financial index lost 1.49 percent to 86,995.93.

Actives were again led by utilities which spearheaded last week's rally. Cukurova Elektrik and Aktas Elektrik were steady at 132,500 and 95,000 lira, respectively while Kepez Elektrik fell 2,500 lira to 115,000. They made up 30.2 percent of the total turnover.
